heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Gabon
heroData.subtitle: Compliant Employment in the CEMAC Zone
heroData.description: Navigate the Gabonese Labor Code with our Employer of Record solution. We handle CNSS/CNAMGS declarations, tax withholding (IRPP), and strict local hiring quotas ('Gabonization') so you can focus on operations.
heroData.bestFor: Oil & Gas, Mining, Forestry, and Tech Expansions

steps.title: Role Classification & Quota Check
steps.description: Before hiring, we verify the role against 'Gabonization' policies. If the role is reserved for locals (e.g., certain HR or administrative positions), an expat hire may be rejected. We assist in classifying the job level (Cadre vs. Non-Cadre) which dictates notice periods and trial durations.

steps.title: Pre-Employment Medical Exam
steps.description: It is mandatory for every employee to undergo a medical examination to certify fitness for work. This must be conducted by an accredited occupational health doctor before the contract commencement or within the trial period.

steps.title: Contract Drafting (French)
steps.description: Drafting the employment contract in French, as required by law. We ensure clauses on place of work, mobility, and trial periods (1-6 months) are compliant. Fixed-term contracts (CDD) must be justified and are limited in duration (2 years max including renewal).

steps.title: CNSS & CNAMGS Registration
steps.description: Registering the employee with the Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS) for pension/family benefits and the Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie et de Garantie Sociale (CNAMGS) for health coverage. This must be done within 8 days of hiring.

steps.title: Tax Identification (NIF)
steps.description: Obtaining the employee's Tax Identification Number (Numéro d'Identification Fiscale) from the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) to facilitate monthly IRPP withholdings.

steps.title: Bank Account Setup
steps.description: Assisting the employee with opening a local bank account (e.g., BGFI, UGB) if they do not have one. Cash payments are restricted for salaries above a certain threshold (usually 100k XAF), favoring bank transfers.

steps.title: Local Handbook Acknowledgement
steps.description: Ensuring the employee signs off on the Internal Regulations (Règlement Intérieur) which covers disciplinary codes, health and safety, and working hours, filed with the Labor Inspectorate.

items.title: Formalities
items.text: Gabonese business culture is formal. Use titles (Monsieur, Madame, Docteur) until invited to use first names. Handshakes are the standard greeting.

items.title: Dress Code
items.text: Business attire is conservative and formal (Suit and tie for men). Dressing well is seen as a sign of respect.

items.title: Hierarchy
items.text: Decision-making is top-down. It is crucial to respect the chain of command and direct important queries to the highest ranking person present.

items.title: Punctuality
items.text: While meetings may start late due to traffic or other factors, foreign partners are expected to be punctual.

items.title: Language
items.text: French is the sole language of business. Contracts, meetings, and marketing materials must be in French. Translators are essential if you are not fluent.

items.title: Relationship Building
items.text: Business moves at the speed of trust. Socializing over meals is common and helps cement relationships before deals are signed.

rows.label: Housing
values: Or actual rent paid if lower (subject to rules). Commonly provided to expats.

rows.label: Car / Transport
values: Company cars for personal use are taxable. Transport allowance (transport personnel) is often exempt up to a limit.

rows.label: CNSS (Social Security)
values: Annual ceiling of 18,000,000 XAF. Includes Family Allowances (11%), Old Age (5%), Occupational Risks (3%), etc.

rows.label: CNAMGS (Health)
values: National Disease Insurance and Social Guarantee Fund. Calculated on gross salary (capped at 2.5M XAF/month).

rows.label: FNH (Housing Fund)
values: Fonds National de l'Habitat. Applies to gross salary.

items.title: Strict Termination Laws
items.text: Terminating an employee is highly regulated. You must have a 'real and serious cause' (cause réelle et sérieuse). Economic dismissal requires authorization from the Labor Inspectorate, which can take months.

items.title: Seniority Bonus
items.text: After 2 years of service, employees are entitled to a seniority bonus (prime d'ancienneté). This is a statutory requirement, not optional, and increases with tenure.

items.title: 13th Month Pay
items.text: While not in the Labor Code, the 13th-month bonus is customary and mandatory under many Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs) in sectors like Oil, Banking, and Comms.

items.title: Foreign Worker Quotas
items.text: Strict enforcement of quotas means EOR for expats is scrutinized. You must prove the unavailability of local skills.

items.title: Remote Work
items.text: Remote work is permitted but not explicitly detailed in the old Labor Code. Contracts should clearly specify the 'place of work' as the employee's home to avoid disputes.

faqs.question: What happens if an employee is sick?
faqs.answer: Employees are entitled to up to 6 months of paid sick leave (depending on tenure). The employer pays a portion, and CNSS may reimburse a part after a certain period.

faqs.question: Can I use EOR to hire sales reps?
faqs.answer: Yes, EOR is excellent for sales reps. However, if they negotiate and sign contracts on your behalf, it creates a Permanent Establishment risk.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum wage?
faqs.answer: Yes, the SMIG (Salaire Minimum Interprofessionnel Garanti) is approximately 150,000 XAF, but most skilled roles command significantly higher market rates.

faqs.question: How are overtime hours paid?
faqs.answer: Overtime is paid at +20% for the first 8 hours/week, +50% beyond that, and +50-100% for weekends/holidays.

faqs.question: Is maternity leave paid?
faqs.answer: Yes, 14 weeks of maternity leave are paid (50% by employer, 50% by CNSS usually, though rules vary by CBA).

faqs.question: What is the probation period?
faqs.answer: 1 month for workers, 3 months for supervisors, 6 months for executives. Specific renewal rules apply.

steps.title: Variable Data Input
steps.description: Collection of variable elements: Overtime, Leave days taken, Bonuses, and Benefits in Kind usage (for tax calculation).

steps.title: Gross Calculation
steps.description: Determining Gross Salary including Base Pay + Seniority Bonus + Allowances + Overtime. Note: Transport allowance up to a certain limit is exempt.

steps.title: Social Deductions (Employee)
steps.description: Deducting CNSS (2.5% capped) and CNAMGS (1% capped) from the Gross to arrive at the Taxable Gross.

steps.title: Tax Calculation (IRPP & TCS)
steps.description: Applying the IRPP progressive scale (0-35%) on Taxable Gross (after 20% pro-expense deduction). Adding TCS (Taxe Complémentaire sur Salaire) of 5% on salaries > 150k.

steps.title: Net Pay Disbursement
steps.description: Transferring Net Pay to employee bank accounts. Payslips must be distributed electronically or physically by the end of the month.

steps.title: Filings & Remittance
steps.description: Declaring and paying withheld taxes to DGI and social contributions to CNSS/CNAMGS by the 15th of the following month.

items.title: TCS Applicability
items.text: The Combined Tax on Salaries (Taxe Complémentaire sur les Salaires - TCS) is 5% and applies to the full salary for anyone earning over 150,000 XAF/month. It is often overlooked but critical.

items.title: Family Quotient
items.text: IRPP is reduced by the 'Quotient Familial' based on the number of dependents (parts). Employees must provide birth certificates to claim this reduction (0.5 share per child).

items.title: Electronic Declarations
items.text: Use the 'e-Tax' (SYGTax) portal for all monthly declarations. Manual filing is being phased out for medium/large enterprises.

items.title: Late Penalties
items.text: Penalties for late payment of CNSS are severe (up to 10% plus daily interest). Automated reminders are essential.

items.title: Professional Expense Allowance
items.text: The 20% deduction for professional expenses is automatic but capped at 10,000,000 XAF per year.

faqs.question: Is the 20% professional expense deduction automatic?
faqs.answer: Yes, for IRPP calculation, you deduct 20% from the gross taxable income (capped at 10M XAF/year) before applying the tax brackets.

faqs.question: Are banking details mandatory on payslips?
faqs.answer: It is best practice to include the IBAN/RIB on the payslip, but the mandatory fields are role, period, gross items, and specific deductions.

faqs.question: How are expats taxed?
faqs.answer: Expats resident in Gabon (>183 days) are taxed on worldwide income. Non-residents are taxed only on Gabon-sourced income, usually via a 20% withholding tax.

faqs.question: Is the 13th month taxable?
faqs.answer: Yes, the 13th month is treated as regular salary and is fully subject to IRPP, TCS, CNSS, and CNAMGS.

faqs.question: How often must we file returns?
faqs.answer: Monthly. The 'DAS' (Annual Declaration of Salaries) is the only annual requirement, due by April 30th.

steps.title: Gross Input
steps.description: Begin with the base monthly gross salary including all fixed monthly allowances.

steps.title: Social Deductions
steps.description: Subtract 2.5% for CNSS and 1.0% for CNAMGS (both subject to monthly income ceilings).

steps.title: Professional Expenses
steps.description: Apply a flat 20% deemed professional expense deduction to the remaining balance before tax.

steps.title: IRPP Calculation
steps.description: Apply the progressive tax brackets (0% to 35%) to the taxable base determined in step 3.

steps.title: TCS & Net Total
steps.description: Subtract 5.0% for the TCS tax on the full gross value to arrive at the final payable Net Salary.

items.title: Ceiling Sensitivity
items.text: CNSS contributions are capped at an annual base of 18M XAF. High-earners will see their net pay increase slightly in Q4 once the ceiling is hit.

items.title: Benefit in Kind Valuation
items.text: Housing and car benefits must be added to the gross taxable base before calculating IRPP, or they will fail an audit.

items.title: 13th Month Impact
items.text: When 13th month is paid, the employee may move into a higher tax bracket for that month, significantly increasing the one-time IRPP withholding.

items.title: Resident vs. Non-Resident
items.text: Non-residents are often subject to a flat 20% withholding instead of the progressive scale, simplifying the calculation for short-term expats.

faqs.question: Does this include the employer share?
faqs.answer: This logic primarily focuses on the gross-to-net transition; however, the employer must budget an additional ~27% for their portion of contributions.

faqs.question: How accurate is the IRPP estimate?
faqs.answer: The estimate is highly accurate for single individuals. Rates may vary slightly if the employee claims and proves multiple dependents (parts).

faqs.question: Is the transport allowance taxable?
faqs.answer: Transport allowances are typically exempt from social security but are often included in the taxable base for IRPP above a certain customary threshold.

faqs.question: What happens in a mid-month hire?
faqs.answer: Calculations are prorated based on the actual number of days worked (usually out of 30), adjusting the tax brackets accordingly.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Gabon
heroData.subtitle: Business Setup via ANPI
heroData.description: Establish a SARL or SA in Gabon compliant with OHADA Uniform Acts. We navigate the 'Guichet Unique' at ANPI-Gabon for swift registration.

steps.title: Notary Engagement
steps.description: Engage a Gabonese notary. Under OHADA law, the company statutes (Articles of Association) must be notarized.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Open a 'compte de constitution' at a local bank (BGFI, UGB) and deposit the share capital (Min 1,000,000 XAF for SARL recommended, though law allows less).

steps.title: Domiciliation
steps.description: Sign a lease agreement or a domiciliation contract for the registered office address. This is required for tax registration.

steps.title: ANPI Submission
steps.description: Submit a complete file to ANPI-Gabon (Agence Nationale de Promotion des Investissements). This includes criminal records of directors, statutes, and lease.

steps.title: Registration Issuance
steps.description: ANPI issues the 'Fiche Circuit' containing the RCCM (Trade Registry) number and NIF (Tax ID) number.

steps.title: Cutter Stamp & Legal Notice
steps.description: Obtain the company seal and publish the incorporation notice in the official gazette or a legal newspaper (e.g., L'Union).

steps.title: Social Security Start
steps.description: Register the company as an employer with CNSS and CNAMGS to enable hiring.

items.title: Overview
items.text: Located 27km from Libreville, Nkok is a world-class industrial zone focused on timber processing, but open to other industries.

items.title: Tax Incentives
items.text: Investors in Nkok enjoy 0% Corporate Income Tax for the first 10 years, followed by a reduced rate of 10% for the next 5 years.

items.title: Customs
items.text: Total exemption from customs duties on imported equipment and raw materials.

items.title: Eligibility
items.text: Requires approval from the GSEZ authority and typically a commitment to local value addition (transformation).

items.title: Libreville
items.text: The political and administrative capital. Home to ANPI, Ministries, and HQs of most service companies. The primary location for interaction with government officials.

items.title: Port-Gentil
items.text: The economic capital. The center of the Oil & Gas and timber industries. Rent and cost of living can be even higher here than in Libreville. Logistics focus.

items.title: Franceville
items.text: Key for mining (Manganese). Located inland at the end of the Trans-Gabon Railway. Growing in importance for infrastructure projects.

items.title: The ANPI Window
items.text: The 'Guichet Unique' theoretically allows 48-hour incorporation. In practice, expect 1-2 weeks for full clearance.

items.title: Business License
items.text: General trading requires a regular license, but sectors like Mining, Oil, and Forestry need specific Ministerial Decrees which take months to obtain.

items.title: OHADA Accounting
items.text: You must appoint an accountant immediately. OHADA requires specific bookkeeping formats that differ from IFRS/GAAP.

heroData.title: Staffing in Gabon
heroData.subtitle: Recruiting for Industry & Services
heroData.description: Find top talent in Libreville and Port-Gentil. We handle the complex visa processes and quota compliance for expat staff while sourcing skilled local professionals.

rows.label: Business Visa
values: Single or Multiple entry. Strictly for meetings/conferences. NO paid work allowed.

rows.label: Work Permit (Autorisation d'Emploi)
values: Issued by Ministry of Labor. Prerequisite for the Work Visa. Employer sponsored.

rows.label: Entry Authorization Visa
values: Used to enter Gabon to finalize residency. Requires approved Work Permit.

rows.label: Residence Card (Carte de Séjour)
values: Renewable. The final document allowing long-term stay and work, issued after biometrics.

rows.label: Exit/Re-entry Visa
values: Required for residents to travel out of and return to Gabon.

rows.label: Seasonal Worker Permit
values: For agriculture or specific short-term industrial projects.

steps.title: Labor Market Test
steps.description: For expat hires, publish the job locally. If no Gabonese candidate is found, file a report to justify foreign hiring.

steps.title: Ministry Submission
steps.description: Submit Work Permit application to Ministry of Labor with the contract, CV, and diplomas. Process takes 4-8 weeks.

steps.title: Visa Application
steps.description: Once Work Permit is approved, apply for the Entry Authorization Visa at the nearest Gabonese Embassy or via E-Visa.

steps.title: Arrival & Medical
steps.description: Upon arrival, the employee undergoes a medical check and biometrics for the Residence Card.

items.title: Omar Bongo University (UOB)

items.title: USTM (Masuku)
items.description: University of Science and Technology of Masuku. The primary source for engineering and technical talent, especially for mining.

items.title: BBS School of Management
items.description: BGFI Business School. Excellent for banking, finance, and management recruits.

items.title: AFRAM (Académie Franco-Américaine)
items.description: Private institution focusing on management and international business.

items.title: Institut des Techniques Avancées (ITA)
items.description: Provides technical training relevant to industry and logistics.

items.title: Institut National des Sciences de Gestion (INSG)
items.description: Specializes in management sciences, feeding the corporate sector.

items.title: Talent Hubs
items.text: Libreville is the hub for services, banking, and government. Port-Gentil is the capital for Oil & Gas and maritime skills.

items.title: CV Verification
items.text: Degree fraud occurs. Always verify diplomas with the issuing university, especially for technical or regulated professions.

items.title: Salary Expectations
items.text: Cost of living in Libreville is high (one of the highest in Africa). Salaries must reflect this. Housing allowances are a major negotiation point.

heroData.title: HRIS in Gabon
heroData.subtitle: Digital HR Management
heroData.description: Deploy HR systems that speak French and calculate XAF taxes correctly.

steps.title: Tax Logic
steps.description: Pre-configured for 2025 IRPP brackets and CNSS ceilings. The system must automatically update when new fiscal laws are gazetted.

steps.title: Leave Accrual
steps.description: Must support the '2 days per month' (24 days/year) accrual logic standard in the Gabonese Labor Code.

steps.title: Reporting
steps.description: Ability to export the 'DIPE' (Document Individuel de Prise en Charge) compatible format for social security declarations.

steps.title: Gabonization Monitoring
steps.description: Tracking of local vs. expat ratios to ensure compliance with sector-specific workforce quotas.

items.title: Biometric Integration
items.text: Physical time clocks are popular in industrial sectors to prevent 'buddy punching' and ensure accurate overtime logs.

items.title: Connectivity
items.text: Ensure your HRIS has a low-bandwidth or offline-first mode for remote mining or forestry sites where internet can be intermittent.

items.title: Data Privacy (CNCPPD)
items.text: HR data storage must comply with Gabon's personal data protection laws. Ensure the system provider is authorized by the CNCPPD.

rows.label: Implementation Fee
values: One-time setup, data migration, and training.

rows.label: Monthly License (per head)
values: SaaS model based on total employee headcount.

rows.label: Local Support Package
values: Annual fee for priority support and legal updates.

faqs.question: Can the system handle multiple currencies?
faqs.answer: Yes, while the primary currency is XAF, the system allows for salary denomination in USD or EUR with automatic conversion.

faqs.question: Is the DIPE format automated?
faqs.answer: The system generates the XML or Excel file required for the CNSS electronic portal, reducing manual entry errors.

faqs.question: Does it track medical exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, automated reminders are set for the mandatory biennial medical examinations for every employee.

faqs.question: Are the payslips compliant with Gabonese law?
faqs.answer: Yes, payslips include all 18+ mandatory fields required by the Labor Inspectorate, including job category and social security numbers.

heroData.title: Accounting in Gabon
heroData.subtitle: OHADA Compliance
heroData.description: Navigate the SYSCOHADA system with expert local accountants.

steps.title: Plan Comptable
steps.description: Strict adherence to the Plan Comptable Général OHADA (PCGO) for all ledger entries.

steps.title: Annual Close
steps.description: The fiscal year must end on December 31st. Financial statements must be finalized by April 30th.

steps.title: Statutory Audit
steps.description: Mandatory for all SAs and for SARLs exceeding specific capital (10M XAF) or turnover (250M XAF) thresholds.

steps.title: Record Retention
steps.description: All physical and digital accounting records must be archived and accessible for a minimum of 10 years per OHADA law.

items.title: HLB Premus
items.description: A prominent local firm with deep ties to the Gabonese industrial sector and international network connections.

items.title: Baker Tilly Gabon
items.description: Highly regarded for audit, tax advisory, and complex corporate restructuring.

items.title: Cabinet d'Audit et d'Expertise Comptable
items.description: Strategically based in Port-Gentil, specializing in the Oil & Gas and Maritime sectors.

items.title: EY / Deloitte / KPMG Network
items.description: The Big 4 operate through local correspondence firms or regional hubs covering the CEMAC zone.

items.title: Uniform Act on Commercial Companies
items.text: Regulates the formation, governance, and dissolution of SA, SARL, and SAS entities across 17 member states.

items.title: Uniform Act on Accounting
items.text: Establishes the harmonized accounting standards and financial reporting requirements (SYSCOHADA).

items.title: Uniform Act on Security Interests
items.text: Governs the legal framework for collateral, mortgages, and pledges used to secure commercial financing.

items.title: Uniform Act on Arbitration
items.text: Provides a robust framework for dispute resolution outside of local court systems, favored by foreign investors.

items.title: Language Requirement
items.text: All statutory books and financial statements must be kept in French. English-only records are deemed inadmissible during audits.

items.title: Software Localization
items.text: Sage 100 is the market leader in Gabon. Cloud solutions like QuickBooks require extensive customization to meet OHADA reporting formats.

items.title: Professional Order (ONEC)
items.text: Ensure your external accountant is a member of the 'Ordre National des Experts-Comptables du Gabon' (ONEC) for legal validity.

faqs.question: Can we use IFRS for local filing?
faqs.answer: No, local filing must follow SYSCOHADA rules. However, you can maintain a dual ledger to facilitate IFRS reporting for group consolidation.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late filing?
faqs.answer: Late filing of the 'Tableau Comptable et Statistique' (TCS) can result in fines ranging from 500,000 to 5,000,000 XAF.

faqs.question: Do we need a local auditor?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you meet the statutory thresholds, you must appoint a 'Commissaire aux Comptes' registered with the Gabonese bar.

faqs.question: Is digital archiving legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the digital archive system ensures data integrity and is registered with the CNCPPD.

items.title: Anti-Corruption & Ethics
items.text: Gabon has strengthened its anti-corruption laws. Strict adherence to local statutes and international standards (like FCPA) is vital for long-term operations.

items.title: Labor Quota Audits
items.text: The Labor Inspectorate conducts random audits to ensure the 90% local workforce target is being met in most sectors.

items.title: Environmental Impact (EIA)
items.text: Industrial and extractive projects must undergo a rigorous Environmental Impact Assessment before an operating license is issued.

items.title: Beneficial Ownership
items.text: New OHADA rules require companies to maintain a register of ultimate beneficial owners, accessible to AML/CFT authorities.

items.title: ANPI-Gabon
items.description: The National Agency for Investment Promotion, serving as the one-stop shop for all business registration and permits.

items.title: CNCPPD
items.description: National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data. Oversees all IT and HR data storage compliance.

items.title: CNSS / CNAMGS
items.description: The dual agencies managing social security and health insurance contributions respectively.

items.title: DGI
items.description: The General Directorate of Taxes, responsible for all fiscal collections and audits.

items.title: AGANOR
items.description: The Gabonese Agency for Standardization, ensuring products meet safety and quality benchmarks.

items.title: ARCEP
items.description: Regulatory Authority for Electronic Communications and Posts, governing the telecom and software sectors.

steps.title: Annual Statutory Audit
steps.description: Engagement of an independent auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) to verify financial integrity and OHADA compliance.

steps.title: Quarterly Regulatory Review
steps.description: Internal audit of HR files, labor quotas, and data privacy logs to ensure no drift from legal mandates.

steps.title: E-Portal Synchronization
steps.description: Verification that all monthly filings on SYGTax and CNSS platforms are synchronized with bank payments.

steps.title: Board Resolution Archiving
steps.description: Ensuring all minutes of the General Assembly are localized and physically stored at the registered office address.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for local quota violation?
faqs.answer: Non-compliance can lead to the suspension of work permits for all expat staff and significant administrative fines.

faqs.question: Does Gabon have a data protection authority?
faqs.answer: Yes, the CNCPPD actively monitors how companies handle employee and customer data, requiring prior declaration of many processing activities.

faqs.question: How often are tax audits conducted?
faqs.answer: Major companies can expect a general tax audit every 3-4 years, while smaller entities may face targeted spot checks.

faqs.question: Are AML filings required for all companies?
faqs.answer: All companies must identify their beneficial owners, but high-value transactions have additional reporting requirements to ANIF (Gabon's FIU).

rows.label: Corporate Income Tax (IS)
values: Standard rate for most commercial and industrial entities.

rows.label: Oil & Gas CIT
values: Specific sector rate for upstream petroleum companies.

rows.label: VAT (TVA)
values: Standard rate on goods and services. Mandatory registration if turnover > 60M XAF.

rows.label: Reduced VAT
values: Applied to essentials like cement, sugar, and medical supplies.

rows.label: WHT on Dividends
values: Applicable on distributions to non-residents, reduced by treaties.

rows.label: WHT on Foreign Services
values: Standard rate on technical fees paid to offshore providers.

steps.title: Monthly VAT Declaration
steps.description: Must be filed and paid by the 20th of the month following the transaction period.

steps.title: Monthly Payroll Taxes (IRPP)
steps.description: IRPP and TCS withholdings must be remitted to the DGI by the 15th of the following month.

steps.title: Annual CIT (IS) Declaration
steps.description: The final tax return and balance payment are due by April 30th each year.

steps.title: Business License (Patente)
steps.description: Annual renewal and payment for the municipal business license are generally due in Q1.

items.title: Transfer Pricing Scrutiny
items.text: The Gabonese tax authority (DGI) is increasingly auditing intra-group transactions. Documentation must prove the 'Arm's Length' principle.

items.title: Tax Holidays (Nkok)
items.text: Companies established in the Nkok SEZ can enjoy up to 10 years of total exemption from corporate and dividend taxes.

items.title: E-Filing (SYGTax)
items.text: Registration on the SYGTax portal is mandatory for all taxpayers monitored by the 'Direction des Grandes Entreprises' (DGE).

items.title: Minimum Flat Tax
items.text: Even loss-making companies must pay a minimum flat tax (IMF) based on 1% of their annual turnover (Min 1M XAF).

faqs.question: Is Gabon a party to tax treaties?
faqs.answer: Yes, Gabon has major treaties with France and other CEMAC member states to prevent double taxation.

faqs.question: What is the GST equivalent in Gabon?
faqs.answer: The equivalent is TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), currently set at a standard rate of 18%.

faqs.question: How are capital gains taxed?
faqs.answer: Capital gains are generally treated as taxable income and subject to the standard CIT rate of 30%.

faqs.question: Can we carry forward tax losses?
faqs.answer: Yes, tax losses can be carried forward for a maximum of 5 consecutive years.

heroData.title: Legal & MSA in Gabon
heroData.subtitle: Contractual Security
heroData.description: Lock in your partnerships with legally sound agreements.

items.title: Registration Mandate
items.text: Specific contracts, such as commercial leases or high-value procurement agreements, must be registered with the Tax Authority to be admissible in a Gabonese court.

items.title: Language Supremacy
items.text: While bilingual contracts are common, the French version will always prevail in case of a legal dispute or administrative review.

items.title: Trial Period Clauses
items.text: Employment contracts must explicitly define the duration of trial periods; otherwise, the employee is deemed to have a permanent 'CDI' status from day one.

items.title: Force Majeure

faqs.question: Is electronic signature valid in Gabon?
faqs.answer: Electronic signatures are recognized under the ARCEP framework, but physical signatures are still preferred for high-stakes governmental contracts.

faqs.question: What is the standard dispute resolution clause?
faqs.answer: Most international firms specify arbitration at the CCJA (Abidjan) under OHADA rules rather than local Gabonese courts.

faqs.question: Are non-compete clauses enforceable?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they are limited in time, geography, and specific to the roles that justify such protection.

faqs.question: How long does contract registration take?
faqs.answer: The 'Enregistrement' process usually takes 48 to 72 hours at the local tax office.

items.title: Cybersecurity Awareness
items.text: Phishing and fraud are rising. Invest in platforms with multi-factor authentication (MFA) as a standard requirement.

items.title: Data Sovereignty

items.title: SME Digitalization
items.text: There is a massive shift toward automating manual bookkeeping, driving demand for simplified ERP solutions for small businesses.

faqs.question: Is cloud software legal for banking?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it requires approval from COBAC (the regional banking regulator) regarding data residency and security.

faqs.question: Can we hire remote developers from Gabon?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is a growing pool of developers in Libreville, though many prefer working through hubs like SING.

faqs.question: Does standard HR software work in Gabon?
faqs.answer: International platforms (like Workday or SAP) work but usually need a local 'Gabonese layer' to handle social security and IRPP.

faqs.question: How is 4G coverage in rural Gabon?
faqs.answer: Coverage is excellent in main provincial capitals but drops significantly in deep forestry zones, where satellite (Starlink) is now preferred.

items.title: WhatsApp Dominance
items.text: WhatsApp is the primary tool for customer interaction in Gabon. Marketing strategies must include a conversational commerce component.

items.title: Cultural Alignment
items.text: Ads should reflect 'Gabonese pride.' Using local slang (Francais Gabonais) and locally-shot visuals significantly increases engagement.

items.title: Outdoor Advertising

items.title: Radio Reach

faqs.question: What is the most popular social media platform?
faqs.answer: Facebook remains the most dominant, followed closely by TikTok and Instagram for younger urban audiences.

faqs.question: Are there advertising taxes?
faqs.answer: Yes, outdoor advertising and TV spots are subject to specific communal and audiovisual taxes.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing effective in Gabon?
faqs.answer: Very. Local influencers in comedy and music have massive reach and high trust levels compared to traditional ads.

faqs.question: Do we need French-only content?
faqs.answer: Yes, French is the language of commerce. English content should only be used if targeting the small expat O&G community.
